I would guess the Sumerians. In their folklore they had the Annunaki, the reptile gods. Seeing something come from the heavens like a meteorite burning up, it could have been seen as a messenger or an omen of some kind. Hence in other religions you have the "chariots of fire" traversing the sky -- usually linked to angels / archangels. Which the most logical explanation would be something burning up in the sky (ie; a meteorite). The mention of Sumerians and dragon tales goes back as far as 5000BC.

If a Sumerian person could have seen a ball of fire leaving a smokey trail in the sky, relating it to a godly act of some kind -- a flying god or messenger of the gods. Given the reptilian gods (the Annunaki) they could have dubbed an event such as a meteorite a breathing flying reptile of some kind. Things that flew across the sky had the tendency to be seen as higher beings, usually godly.

Another aspect could be related to volcanic rubble being spewed into the air, interpreted as a godly creature emerging. Hence our concept of dragons living inside of volcanoes in popular lore.

The fire breathing dragon that destroyed villages could have been tales of volcanic eruptions simply being hit by rubble and hot ash, amidst all the chaos the people of the time could have thought they were being attacked by a fire breathing flying monster.
